warning.content:
ENES is applicable for any Engine that requires a Shop Visit that: (i) occurs within the EFH limits as
detailed in the table below; (ii) does not require a performance restoration Workscope and/or FFP
Workscope; (iii) is charged on a Time and Materials basis ; and (iv) is not eligible for any other CFM
Special Guarantees and warranties, ("ENES Shop Visit").
For any ENES Shop Visit performed under this Service Agreement, CFM will provide a discount in
the form of a CFM credit note corresponding to a fifty percent (50%) discount of new parts (non-LLP)
and RPL price items during the first EFH Limit 1 set forth in the table below. Thereafter, such
discounts will decrease on a pro rata basis from EFH Limit 1 to zero percent (0%) at the EFH Limit
2.
For the Group1 only, the fifty percent (50%) discount described above will be available up to EFH
Limit 3 for any removal due to reduced durability linked to early engine configuration.

earning.comments:
The LLP Variable Credit Discount in respect of a qualifying Engine pursuant to Article 7.3.1 shall be an
amount equal to thirty percent (30%) of the Net LLP Price prorated by the number of LLP cycles
remaining on such removed LLP until its life expiry, up to twelve thousand (12,000) LLP cycles (the
"LLP Variable Credit Discount").
For the purpose of this Article, the "Net LLP Price" means the then-year price invoiced by CFM and paid
by Customer for the new Fan and LPT LLP replacing the Removed LLP, net of any LLP discounts
received under this Service Agreement or any other agreement with CFM. The LLP Variable Credit
Discount will be made available as a credit and shall be applied against the supplemental invoice for
the new Fan & LPT LLP purchased by Customer to replace the Removed LLP on the same Engine.
If any Removed LLP is evaluated to be Scrapped Parts or Unserviceable, no applicable LLP Variable
Credit Discount shall be provided. Inspection and repair of the Removed LLP is at CFM's cost.
earning.label: LLP Variable CREDIT DISCOUNT

earning.comments:
Customer shall earn a LLP Variable Credit Discount per Engine upon satisfaction of the following
requirements:
a) completion of title transfer of the Removed LLP to CFM; and
b) completion of the shop visit for the Engine at which the Removed LLP is replaced with new LLP.
In the event, that the LLP Variable Credit Discount had been issued and applied by the Customer and
is not earnt pursuant to the above, then such issued but unearned LLP Variable Credit Discount shall
be refunded in full to CFM within thirty (30) calendar days of a notice in respect of the same.
In no event, shall CFM pay Customer for the same event or occurrence under this LLP Variable Credit
Discount and any other single Engine warranty or guarantee. In no event shall Customer claim the LLP
Variable Credit Discount more than once for each Removed LLP.
earning.label: LLP Variable Credit Discount - Earning

earning.comments:
The Parties acknowledge and agree that if any Fan LLP or LPT LLP (as defined in Chapter 5 of the
Engine Shop Manual) is removed and replaced during a shop visit under this Service Agreement
("Removed LLP") in order to meet Customer's obligation to replace at least one (1) whole stack of LLP
for each Engine during its relevant Coverage Period pursuant to Article 6.4 below, then:
a. title to the Removed LLP shall pass to CFM upon its removal from the relevant Engine during a
shop visit; and
b. CFM will grant Customer a LLP Variable Credit Discount (as defined and calculated below), subject
to the following conditions:
i. the Engine from which the Removed LLP is removed is covered under the 9Y Coverage Period;
ii. such Removed LLP is Serviceable and has a minimum of ten thousand (10,000) LLP cycles
remaining; and
iii. Customer providing CFM with all such required records and documentation in relation to the
Removed LLP pursuant to Article 7.3.4 to the satisfaction of CFM.
earning.label: Removed LLP Transfer & Conditions for LLP Variable Credit Discount Issuance

referential.article:
CFM will provide Services in accordance with the specific Workscope identified in the Service Agreement.
Workscope is the document written by CFM and agreed upon by both CFM and Customer, describing the
repair or approach to repair of Engine to meet the requirements of the Repair Specification. CFM will
develop the Workscope to include Service Bulletins for that specific Workscope.

Customer's agreement shall be required for any proposed Service Bulletin. Customer shall not be liable to 
pay any costs in relation to any such Service Bulletin that it has not agreed.

CFM shall charge Customer for any additional work requirements above the FFP Workscope requested by Customer, or directed by Customer's specific maintenance manuals or Repair Specification, which exceed the FFP Workscope defined by CFM.

Customer shall provide CFM with adequate information of its Engine Shop Visit planning, {forecasts with
relevant ESN, updated at least [period],} specifying projected requirements to cover at least the following [months_following] months period. 
{On a monthly basis, Customer will share detailed forecast Shop-Visit, plan for the following [months] months. In parallel CFM and Customer shall exchange Customer's MRO capability development plans and progress}
CFM reserves the right to postpone Induction of any Engine should Customer fail to provide adequate information on its forecasted removal schedule and/or to use a previously allocated slot.

Should Customer cancel any shop visit {[1] through a written prior notice given} [operator] [months] months before the shop visit scheduled date, CFM will issue to Customer an invoice of [amount1] [currency] {In case of no prior written notice or a prior written notice given less than [months] months before the shop visit scheduled date, }{CFM will issue to Customer an invoice of [amount2] [currency2].}

Customer will delegate to CFM approval of all DICA (Deviation of Instruction for Continuous Airworthiness) / DR (Departure Record) which do not include any follow-up inspection, repair or part replacement on-wing. CFM will have to obtain written approval from Customer to accept a DICA/DR with a follow-up requirement on-wing. {Customer agrees to respond to CFM's request within [Business_day]
Business Day to confirm approval.}

In the event Non-OEM Parts or Non-OEM Repairs are exposed during the shop visit, CFM will replace the corresponding parts, on a Time and Material Basis with OEM hardware. Customer will be notified of the disposition and an alternate solution may be proposed to Customer. LLP hardware operated with influencing Non-OEM Parts or Non-OEM Repairs per Chapter 5 of the appropriate CFM approved shop manual and any relevant Service Bulletin concerning Critical Influencing Parts will be considered influenced by unknown operational conditions and replacement will be made by CFM on a Time and Material Basis. Any resulting adverse effects to Engine TAT at the shop will be mutually agreed, and the original TAT (if any) will be increased by the agreed Days. Non-OEM Parts or Non-OEM Repairs that are not exposed during a shop visit shall remain in an Engine. If, however, these and any other Non-OEM Parts or Non-OEM Repairs, or LLP hardware operated with influencing Non-OEM Parts or Non-OEM Repairs, cause an Unserviceable condition or Engine removal, the costs associated with such events will not be covered by the warranties provided in this Service Agreement.

remedy as liquidated damages:

("TOW") guarantee as described in Article "Time On Wing ("TOW") Guarantee" below for the repaired

This Services warranty is applicable only if the Engine/Parts, following Redelivery,

(a) has been transported, stored, installed, operated, handled, maintained, repaired in accordance with the then-current CFM recommendations as stated in AMM or CFM manuals, Airworthiness Directives, Service Bulletins, and other relevant written instructions

(b) has not been altered, modified or repaired by anyone other than the CFM Designated Repair Station; and 

(c) has not been subjected to accident, misuse, abuse or neglect.

{[2] Any warranty for warranted Parts will be the warranty, if any, of the manufacturer of such warranted Parts.}

{[1] Any warranty for Engines or parts, Engine Controls and Accessories, components and material thereof,
including the design, material or engineering defects of a manufacturer, will be the warranty, if any, of
the manufacturer of such Engines or parts, Engine Controls and Accessories, components or material
thereof.
The foregoing will constitute the sole remedy of Customer and the sole liability of CFM for defective
workmanship relative to the Engines. The liability of CFM connected with or resulting from the Services
warranty shall not in any event exceed the cost of correcting the defect as provided above, and, upon
the expiration of the shortest period described therein, all such liability will terminate. In no event shall
CFM be liable for any special, expectation, consequential, incidental, resultant, indirect, punitive or
exemplary damages (including loss of use, loss of profit or loss of revenue in connection with the
Engines).}

Customer may not assign the Services warranty without CFM’s prior written consent. However, CFM will consent to a Services warranty assignment to Customer’s lessor upon written request, subject to the terms and conditions of a mutually agreed warranty assignment letter.

Customer will assure that any requested repair of an Engine, accessory or component that is covered under a third party warranty that is not assigned to CFM will be performed directly by that person at no expense to CFM. Notwithstanding the above, CFM may accept a purchase order for the time and material repair of a warranted item from Customer or the person giving the warranty.

referential.article:
CFM agrees to provide, for a period of twelve (12) years commencing upon the entry into revenue
service of each Engine (the "Guarantee Period"), the following extended new engine support (the
"ENES") to Customer in support of the Engines.
For the purpose of the article the "Group1" means the following thirty (30) ESNs into the table below:

Group 1 :

603486 | 603304 | 603026
603516 | 603338 | 603035
603553 | 603359 | 603079
603554 | 603364 | 603107
603561 | 603373 | 603148
603574 | 603385 | 603161
603622 | 603407 | 603163
603602 | 603409 | 603198
603607 | 603437 | 603283
603625 | 603441 | 603294

ENES is applicable for any Engine that requires a Shop Visit that: (i) occurs within the EFH limits as
detailed in the table below; (ii) does not require a performance restoration Workscope and/or FFP
Workscope; (iii) is charged on a Time and Materials basis ; and (iv) is not eligible for any other CFM
Special Guarantees and warranties, ("ENES Shop Visit").
For any ENES Shop Visit performed under this Service Agreement, CFM will provide a discount in
the form of a CFM credit note corresponding to a fifty percent (50%) discount of new parts (non-LLP)
and RPL price items during the first EFH Limit 1 set forth in the table below. Thereafter, such
discounts will decrease on a pro rata basis from EFH Limit 1 to zero percent (0%) at the EFH Limit
2.
For the Group1 only, the fifty percent (50%) discount described above will be available up to EFH
Limit 3 for any removal due to reduced durability linked to early engine configuration.


CFM Engine model : LEAP-1B27
EFH ("EFH Limit 1") : 8,000 Engine Flight Hours since New
EFH ("EFH Limit 1") : 10,000 Engine Flight Hours since New
EFH ("EFH Limit 1") : 15,000 Engine Flight Hours since New


The ENES shall not apply to Parts:

i. Listed in the ATA Chapters from 73 to 80, except for those Engine parts listed that are sold
directly by CFM to Customer;
ii. That are procured directly by the Customer from Suppliers and which are covered by Supplier
warranty and/or the CFM "Suppliers Back-up Warranty" pursuant to the GTA.
iii. Replaced at Customer convenience or discretion contrary to CFM recommendations (e.g.,
Category 7 SB Parts not on attrition);
iv. LLP replacement for life expiration.
The ENES is subject to conditions stipulated under Exhibit "Basis And Conditions For Special
Guarantees".

In concideration of Customer taking delivery of Aircraft and Spare Engines in accordance with the
Delivery Schedule and Spare Engines Delivery Schedule respectively as described in the Exhibit
"Covered Engines and Operating Parameters" CFM agrees to provide the ENES at no charge to
Customer during the Guarantee Period.

A. Customer shall submit any claim pursuant to this Article "Extended New Engine Support" to CFM
warranty administration duly substantiated by an invoice of the Parts claimed, including reference
number of this Service Agreement, ESN, engine flight hours since new and engine flight cycles
since new at QSV induction, QSV date completion. Any part replaced by this program shall be
delivered to CFM, and shall become CFM property.
Any claim submitted one (1) year after the Guarantee Period expiration shall be considered null
and void.
In case such data are not provided, or are provided incomplete by Customer in the due time, CFM
shall reject the relevant claim.
